Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-'Uyun) on Surah 109, verses 1–6:

(p-357) Surat al-Kafirun

Makkiyyah according to Ibn Mas'ud, al-Hasan and 'Ikrimah; Madaniyyah according to one of the two opinions of Ibn 'Abbas, and of Qatadah and al-Dahhak.

﴿Say: O you who disbelieve,﴾ and the verses. Muhammad ibn Ishaq mentioned that the occasion of its revelation was: "al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, al-'As ibn Wa'il, al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib and Umayyah ibn Khalaf met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Muhammad, come, worship what we worship, and we will worship what you worship, and we will share with you in all our affairs. If what you have brought is better than what is in our hands, we will have shared in it with you and taken our portion of it; and if what is in our hands is better than what is in your hands, you will have shared with us in our affair and taken your portion of it.' So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Say: O you who disbelieve,﴾."

The imperative particle in this surah, in Surat al-Ikhlas and in al-Mu'awwidhatayn is recited (as it stands), because they were revealed as answers. By "the disbelievers" He means specific people, not all disbelievers, because among them were those who believed and worshipped Allah, and among them were those who died or were killed upon their disbelief; these are the ones addressed by this statement, and among them are those who are mentioned.

﴿I do not worship what you worship﴾, meaning the idols.

﴿Nor do you worship what I worship﴾, meaning Allah alone, and the verses.

If it is said: What is the benefit of this repetition? It is said: In it there are two aspects:

The first: His saying at the beginning ﴿I do not worship﴾ and (you do not worship) refers to the present, and His second saying refers to the future; this was said by al-Akhfash.

The second: The first, in His saying ﴿I do not worship﴾ and ﴿nor do you﴾ and the verse, refers to the future, and the second is a report about him and about them in the past; so this is not a repetition, due to the difference in what is intended by them.

If it is said: Why did He say (what I worship) and not (who I worship)? It is said: Because it corresponds to His saying: ﴿Nor am I a worshipper of what you have worshipped﴾, and these are idols and images, and only (what) is suitable for them, not (who); so the second was made to conform to the first, so that the speech would correspond and not conflict.

﴿For you is your religion, and for me is my religion﴾. In it there are two aspects:

The first: For you is your religion which you hold, which is disbelief, and for me is my religion which I hold, which is Islam; this was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: For you is the recompense of your deeds, and for me is the recompense of my deeds.

This is a threat from Him to them, and its meaning is: and the recompense of my deed is sufficient as a reward; this was said by Ibn 'Isa.

Ibn 'Abbas said: There is no surah in the Qur'an more grievous to the anger of Iblis than this surah, because it is monotheism and disavowal of shirk.
